topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class to the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional modalities, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and multidrug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional cancer management approaches including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting hormone dependence, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapeutic strategies exploit intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities such as hormone signaling pathways, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, clinical mechanisms, and complex resistance and addiction pathways associated with targeted kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the engineering and therapeutic application of monoclonal antibodies to directly inhibit receptor signaling or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy, immune checkpoint blockade, and adoptive cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and detail strategies to harness or engineer T cells to eliminate malignant cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future paradigms in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize overarching therapeutic challenges, historical changes in cancer mortality, and future clinical paradigms.
